newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine Congress approves mortgage bank sale.
newsitem.headline: Argentine Congress approves mortgage bank sale.

text.p: The Argentine Senate approved late on Wednesday the privatisation of state mortgage bank Banco Hipotecario Nacional, which now only needs presidential approve to become law.
The ruling Peronist Party's majority in the upper house of parliament ensured that the bill, which was approved by deputies in May, was passed by 32 votes in favor to four against and one abstention.
President Carlos Menem hopes the sale will raise at least $3 billion which he will use to fund construction, housing and infrastructure projects.

The law will provide for the creation of a Trustee Fund for Regional Infrastructure which will administer the privatization funds. It must put aside $100 million for the building of homes for which loans of up to 95 percent will be available. The rest of the revenue will be for infrastructure projects, half going to the provincial governments and half to central government.

The Peronist head of the Budget and Finance Committee of the Senate, Carlos Verna, told the house: "This privatization is different to the rest, because it sets aside the funds, and maintains a function for the bank, for building homes for the people."
